reason: Driven and measured, not read; the occlusion reproduces exactly and I could not kill it. At 1440x960, 1280x900, 1279x800, 1152x800 and 1024x800, on ?v=paper AND ?v=ink, opening the FIRST moment of owner-flight ("Menu tasting at The Orchard") and pressing +7: .b-edit computed padding-top 88px, content width 310px, .b-undoText wraps to two lines (textH 45, line-height 22.5) so the bar is 94px (45 text + 8 gap + 28 .b-undoAct + 12 pad + 1 hairline), its bottom lands at panel-top+111 against a reserve of 88, and the first .b-label ("What it is", top panel-top+89, height 15.4) is 22px INSIDE it. The bar's computed background-color is rgb(255,255,255) on paper and rgb(17,17,17) on ink with no background-image, so it does not veil the label, it paints it out: document.elementFromPoint at the label's own centre returns .b-undo|DIV and at the label's left edge returns .b-undoAct|BUTTON, on both grounds at all five widths. Screenshots of the clipped panel confirm it by eye - the title input sits under an opaque plate with no label while WHEN two rows down keeps its label and its air, and on ink the plate reads as a hole cut through the panel's fore-06 wash. Nothing else reserves for it: reserveUndo() (render-b.js ~1116) early-returns unless getComputedStyle(bar).position === 'fixed', which is only the closed-editor dock below 1024, and the desk rule (b.css ~1494) only sets position:relative/inset:auto/overflow:visible/max-height:none - the panel cannot scroll the label back. It is not in SETTLED: editor-opens-on-a-hole, editor-opens-on-an-empty-88px-band, editor-reserve-is-a-void and the-editor-opens-on-an-empty-band all argue the EMPTY band is a void and ask for the reserve to be REMOVED; this is the opposite objection, that the reserve is too small once the bar fills. Neither gate can see it and I verified why: interaction-check.mjs's band loops (l.953, l.1240) drive state=owner-editing, whose moment is "Send the invitations" - a one-line sentence, bar 71.5px, bottom panel-top+88.5 - so the gate presses +7 at 390/768/1280/1440 and never once meets a two-line bar; its assertions are only 'inside the editor' and 'never on the count', both of which the covering bar still satisfies. TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE FINDING, one narrowing and one widening, neither of which saves it. Narrowing: 'open any moment' is false. The trigger is the sentence exceeding one line at 310px. Of the seven titles, only "Menu tasting at The Orchard" wraps on the move grammar (+7 and -1 both measured at 94px / air -22); the other five give 71.5px and clear the label by 0.5px - which is its own defect, 0.5px of air where the panel's own first label is designed to have 22 (measured air above the three labels at rest: 22, 12, 23.8). But the covering case is not exotic: it is the top row of the default owner plan, and the visibility grammar covers on ordinary titles too - Hidden on "Send the invitations" gives "Send the invitations is now hidden from guests.", 94px, air -22, elementFromPoint .b-undo, both grounds. Widening: the finding UNDERSTATES the coarse-pointer path. It says 390 merely loses its air. Measured at 390x844 with touch, both grounds: the move grammar gives 87.5px and 0.5px air as claimed, but the Hidden grammar on the same first moment gives a 110px bar (44px .b-undoAct under the coarse rule), bottom at panel-top+127 against the 104 reserve, air -22, elementFromPoint .b-undo - the phone erases the label as well. 768 is clean (710px content, bar 57-80.4, air 7.6-31). The proposed fix, driven verbatim: clamp + [data-medium="full"] .b-editHost .b-edit { padding-top: 132px } restores air 22 and elementFromPoint .b-label on both grammars at 1440 and 1024 on both grounds, and the text is not clipped (scrollHeight === clientHeight at 2 lines). Two flaws in it, both fixable and neither fatal, corrected in sharpenedFix: the coarse arithmetic is wrong (16+88+22=126 under-reserves by 22 and leaves the 390 erasure exactly as it is - the coarse worst case is 110, so 148), and 132 makes the rail column overflow so the panel and its steppers re-anchor 18px upward on the first press. I measured that threshold: padding-top 88/96/104/110 shift 0, 116 -2, 124 -10, 132 -18. Real, specific, visible in two screenshots, present in both rooms and on both pointer paths, and invisible to both gates.
sharpenedFix: Keep the finding's structure, correct its two numbers, and let the founder pick the air. (1) Bound the bar - this part is unconditional and free: `.b-edit .b-undoText { display:-webkit-box; -webkit-box-orient:vertical; -webkit-line-clamp:2; overflow:hidden; }`. The span stays in the DOM so role=status still speaks the whole sentence, and at two lines nothing is actually clipped today (scrollHeight === clientHeight); it only stops a long owner-typed title from ever making a fourth row. (2) Reserve the bound height, with the corrected coarse figure: `[data-medium="full"] .b-editHost .b-edit { padding-top: 132px }` (16 + 94 + 22) and, under @media (pointer: coarse), `.b-edit { padding-top: 148px }` - 16 + 110 + 22, NOT the finding's 126, because the coarse action row is 44px not 28 and the measured two-line bar at 332px content is 110px. 126 leaves the 390 Hidden case erasing the label unchanged. (3) Pin the hairline so the air does not breathe between 22 and 44 as the sentence changes length: `[data-medium="full"] .b-editHost .b-edit .b-undo { min-height: 94px }` and, under coarse, `min-height: 110px`. The bar already has align-items:flex-start, so a one-line sentence simply leaves the plate taller; the hairline and the first label then sit at one constant place in every state, which is what the reserve was always for. (4) State the cost honestly, because it is larger than the finding admits. The resting band grows 88 -> 132 at desk and 104 -> 148 on the phone, and at 1440x960 the taller panel overflows the rail column so the panel re-anchors 18px upward on the first press - measured threshold: shift is 0 at padding-top 110, -2 at 116, -10 at 124, -18 at 132. That is a one-time 18px move of the steppers under the pointer, the exact property the 88 was protecting. Two honest ways out, founder's call: (a) take the 18px - it happens once, on the first press, and never again, and it is a smaller harm than an opaque plate deleting the field's name; or (b) hold the reserve at 110 (measured shift 0, air 22.5 on the one-line bar) and clamp the sentence to ONE line at desk, which removes the erasure at zero movement but truncates the delta off the end of long titles. If neither is acceptable, the finding's own alternative is the right answer and it is a build, not this round's: put the bar in flow as the panel's first row. Note that on the coarse path that build is nearly free - .b-edit below 1024 is already bottom-anchored (position:fixed; bottom:12px), so an in-flow bar at its top grows the sheet upward and cannot move the stepper at all until the 72dvh cap is hit.
